claim: The tested OE implementation has lower performance during adaptation than PPO-DR.
limit: One simulator, these settings/budgets and fixed T2/T3 environments. AUC includes starting performance and is not isolated adaptation speed.

claim: Separately tuned OE under varied training scores below separately tuned OE-fixed.
limit: OE mutation SD differs between regimes. The comparison includes separate tuning; it does not identify environmental variation as the sole causal factor.

claim: The PPO-DR versus PPO-fixed directional hypothesis is not supported under its registered rule.
limit: Not proof of equality, no benefit of variation, or failure of domain randomization generally. Hyperparameters differ between regimes.

claim: ES-DR has a small adaptation-AUC advantage over ES-fixed, below the registered margin.
limit: Later addendum, separately tuned settings. Does not by itself support Milano direction on their zero-shot robustness concept.

claim: ES-DR has higher T1 zero-shot normalized competence than ES-fixed.
limit: Later addendum and separate tuning; directional agreement with prior work in a different task, not a direct replication or selection-mechanism test.

claim: The registered absolute-effect comparison labels method as larger than variety.
limit: Interaction CI excludes zero. These are contrasts between separately tuned pipelines, not isolated causal effects of method or variation.

claim: The ES fixed/varied difference exceeds the OE fixed/varied difference.
limit: Separate tuning and the later addendum limit causal interpretation; no selection-mechanism isolation.
